meta.note: Pattern-strategy skill library (paper Sec. 4.2). Entries marked source=seed are textbook transformations offered as untested suggestions: they carry zero occurrences and zero confidence and must earn their statistics from real runs, exactly like a learned entry. Entries gain occurrences, SEC-pass counts and a mean relative advantage A_i as the loop runs, and are demoted to status=invalid if they break equivalence more often than not.

skills.pattern: High-fanout operand driving multiplier with 38+ loads
skills.strategy: Replicate operand registers to split fanout
skills.rationale: A single register driving 38 gates requires large width and exhibits heavy transitional delay. Two identical registers halve the per-register load; synthesis can distribute the multiplier inputs across both copies, reducing driver-to-load capacitance and slew on each path through the Wallace tree.

skills.pattern: carry propagation in sequential 40-bit additions
skills.strategy: unable to reduce depth safely while maintaining equivalence
skills.rationale: Three 40-bit additions (s0+s1, s2+s3, then those two) form 22-stage carry chains. Parallel prefix or carry-save approaches either require hand-coded complex adders (no synthesis guarantee) or change overflow truncation behavior, breaking bit-exact equivalence. Reordering violates the 2-cycle latency constraint.

skills.pattern: Carry propagation in 40-bit final accumulate
skills.strategy: No equivalent optimization available
skills.rationale: Carry-save 3:2 compression was attempted in iteration 1, SEC-passed but synthesized to slower hardware. The balanced tree structure is already standard practice. Ripple carry depth is inherent to the 4-term 40-bit sum without algorithmic restructuring.

skills.pattern: Mux selecting output of wide parallel adders
skills.strategy: Move select to operands before single addition
skills.rationale: Eliminates one full 1024-bit carry chain; input muxes are shallower than two parallel carries plus output selection. Expected saving: ~45% of adder depth.

skills.pattern: Output multiplexer selecting wide arithmetic results
skills.strategy: Move mux before computation into single path
skills.rationale: Eliminates duplicate carry chains. Input multiplexers have shallower propagation delay than output selection after two wide adders. Synthesis can then optimize a single arithmetic datapath, reducing critical-path depth and area.

skills.pattern: Output mux in series with carry chain
skills.strategy: Move mux to inputs; merge dual additions into one
skills.rationale: The result mux in the current code forces both carry chains to complete before selection. Muxing inputs first and performing one addition removes the output mux from the critical path and permits the synthesizer to optimize a single wide-adder datapath rather than two parallel adders.

skills.pattern: 40-bit saturation comparison after accumulation
skills.strategy: Remove unused saturation parameters to prevent inadvertent synthesis
skills.rationale: The SAT_MAX, SAT_MIN, and LIMIT parameters are defined but never used in the RTL. The sat_flag is always 0, and sat_val is just s3 with no actual saturation logic. These unused parameters may trigger synthesis to generate unnecessary comparison logic on the critical path.

skills.pattern: Serial 4-term adder chain instead of balanced tree
skills.strategy: Restructure accumulate as binary tree to parallelize carry
skills.rationale: Original s3 = ((s0+p1)+p2)+p3 chains three 40-bit ripple carries in series, a critical depth-3 dependency. Rebalanced s3 = (s01||s23) + s3 runs p0+p1 and p2+p3 in parallel, then combines them, reducing critical carry-propagation path from 3 sequential adders to 2, cutting depth by ~33%. The carry chain depth is the dominant delay in stages 50-91, so this directly shortens the path.

skills.pattern: 40-bit carry propagation in balanced adder tree
skills.strategy: Unable to optimize while maintaining fixed latency
skills.rationale: The 40-bit additions require full carry propagation. A balanced tree (2 levels) is already optimal for this width without adding pipeline stages. Carry-save would add complexity and isn't safely equivalent given the constraints.

skills.pattern: 40-bit carry ripple in balanced accumulator tree
skills.strategy: No further transformation valid under constraints
skills.rationale: RTL already uses optimal balanced tree; carry-save compression was attempted and synthesized slower; delay spread evenly offers no local fix point; 2-cycle latency constraint prevents pipelining or topology restructuring.

skills.pattern: Dual parallel carries selected by output mux
skills.strategy: Optimize carry propagation depth without repositioning
skills.rationale: Local carry-chain restructuring (carry-save, look-ahead) does not reduce critical path when the bottleneck is output mux placement. Delay is distributed across many pipeline stages rather than concentrated in a reducible hot cell that mux relocation can bypass.

skills.pattern: Serial accumulation chain with 4 operands
skills.strategy: Rebalance serial add chain into binary tree
skills.rationale: Three-stage ripple-carry chain (3 adders deep) becomes two stages (2 adders deep) by computing p0+p1 and p2+p3 in parallel, then combining. Each 40-bit adder carries ~5-8 gate delays; removing one stage recovers ~0.4 ns on the critical path and closes the -0.3573 ns slack shortfall.

skills.pattern: Carry propagation in accumulator tree
skills.strategy: Replace multi-level add tree with carry-save 3:2 compression
skills.rationale: Current balanced tree synthesizes to serial carry-propagation: two 40-bit adds (s01, s23) feed a third. Carry-save reduces three adds (depth 2x single-add) to one: a constant-depth 3:2 compressor producing (sum, carry) pair, followed by one final carry-propagate add. Depth halves.

skills.pattern: Sign-extension through intermediate wires in adder tree
skills.strategy: Inline sign-extension expressions to reduce intermediate nodes
skills.rationale: The current design explicitly creates four 40-bit sign-extended versions (s0–s3) of the 32-bit products before adding them. These intermediate wires add routing delay and potential gate duplication. Inlining the sign-extension concatenations directly into the addition expressions eliminates the intermediate nodes, allowing synthesis to better optimize the critical datapath through the accumulator tree.

skills.pattern: 1024-bit carry propagation in muxed addition
skills.strategy: No optimization found within fixed-latency constraint
skills.rationale: Carry-save or restructuring approaches require either a final full-width adder (same critical path) or pipeline stages (disallowed). The 1024-bit addition is fundamental; moving the mux position does not reduce sequential path depth. Delay is spread evenly across 262 stages rather than concentrated in a reducible hot cell.

skills.pattern: 512-bit serial parity reduction
skills.strategy: replace serial XOR chain with balanced tree
skills.rationale: Serial chain is O(n) depth; balanced tree reduces to O(log n). For 512 bits, 512 stages → 9 stages, eliminating the ripple delay through independent bit positions.

skills.pattern: arithmetic operator chain split across a module boundary
skills.strategy: keep the whole chain in one hierarchy so it can merge
skills.rationale: Hierarchy is a hard boundary for operator merging. A multiply in one module feeding an add in its parent cannot become a single compression tree, however obviously the two belong together.

skills.pattern: carry propagation across a wide accumulator
skills.strategy: accumulate in carry-save form and resolve with a single carry-propagate adder
skills.rationale: Each full-width add resolves a carry chain. Keeping the running total as a redundant (sum, carry) pair makes every intermediate add a constant-depth 3:2 compression, and only the last step pays for a carry chain.
skills.example:
// keep {s, c} redundant through the chain, resolve once at the end
wire [W:0] total = s + c;

skills.pattern: deep FSM or decode logic
skills.strategy: pre-decode the next state one cycle early and register the decoded form
skills.rationale: Decoding a binary state register into control signals puts a decoder in series with everything it controls. Registering the decoded (one-hot) form moves the decode off the consuming path without adding latency, because the decode of the *next* state is computable this cycle.

skills.pattern: Deep multi-level ripple adder chain in accumulator
skills.strategy: Replace serial ripple levels with carry-save 3:2 compression
skills.rationale: Three cascaded 40-bit ripple additions (52 AOI/OAI cells, ~66 gate stages) was targeted for replacement with constant-depth 3:2 carry-save compression using XOR for sum and majority for carry. However, this breaks equivalence, suggesting the custom accumulation logic depends on intermediate carry propagation patterns or the accumulator state update rule is not commutative with carry representation.

skills.pattern: hand-instantiated arithmetic component
skills.strategy: use the inferred operator so the tool picks the architecture
skills.rationale: An explicitly instantiated adder or multiplier is a black box with a fixed architecture. The inferred operator lets synthesis choose one suited to its context and merge it with its neighbours.

skills.pattern: high-fanout signal on the critical path
skills.strategy: replicate the driver so each load group has its own copy
skills.rationale: A net driving many loads needs a big driver or a buffer tree; both cost delay on the launching path. Duplicating the logic that produces it splits the load without changing the value.
skills.example:
reg sel_a, sel_b;  // two copies of one condition
always @(posedge clk) begin sel_a <= cond; sel_b <= cond; end

skills.pattern: intermediate arithmetic result truncated between operators
skills.strategy: widen the intermediate so the operator chain stays one datapath
skills.rationale: Assigning a product-plus-sum to a narrower wire and widening again downstream splits one arithmetic block into two, each optimised alone, so no compression tree spans them. Tool-dependent: a flow without a datapath extractor gains nothing here, and there narrowing to the width the data provably occupies can instead be the winning move.
skills.example:
wire [15:0] t = a * b + c;   // splits the datapath
wire [16:0] t = a * b + c;   // keeps it whole

skills.pattern: long path through an operand shared by many consumers
skills.strategy: isolate the operand per consumer so an idle consumer stops loading it
skills.rationale: Operand isolation removes both switching power and capacitive load from the shared net, shortening the path that drives it.
skills.example: wire [W-1:0] op_for_b = en_b ? shared : {W{1'b0}};

skills.pattern: loop-carried dependency in a generate loop
skills.strategy: reduce with a balanced tree instead of a linear scan
skills.rationale: A generate loop whose body consumes the previous iteration's output elaborates into a chain as deep as the trip count. A priority cascade, a ripple carry and a shift chain are all written this way. The source shows one assignment and synthesis produces N levels, which is why reading the code does not reveal it.

skills.pattern: mixed signed and unsigned operands in one expression
skills.strategy: make signedness explicit and consistent across the expression
skills.rationale: A signed subexpression combined with an unsigned one forces two operator implementations where one would serve, and puts conversion logic on the path between them.

skills.pattern: mux-heavy selection logic
skills.strategy: flatten the serial mux chain into a single balanced select
skills.rationale: Nested conditionals synthesise to a chain of 2:1 muxes with depth equal to the nesting. A one-hot or case-based select of the same conditions gives one balanced level of selection instead.

skills.pattern: priority encoder or leading-one chain
skills.strategy: reduce with a balanced tree instead of a linear priority scan
skills.rationale: A linear priority chain has depth proportional to width. A tree reduction that combines (found, index) pairs pairwise has logarithmic depth and the same result.
skills.example: // combine pairwise: (found_hi ? idx_hi : idx_lo) up the tree

skills.pattern: register placed inside an arithmetic chain
skills.strategy: register the datapath output and let retiming place it
skills.rationale: A flop between two operators stops them being merged, so each is implemented separately and no carry architecture can be chosen across the pair. Registering the end of the chain and letting retiming move the boundary gives the same latency and a better structure.

skills.pattern: reset logic in series with the datapath
skills.strategy: move the reset out of the data path and onto the register's own reset
skills.rationale: A reset ANDed into the data expression puts a gate in series with the whole datapath. Using the flop's reset port keeps the datapath clean.

skills.pattern: saturation or clamp after a long arithmetic path
skills.strategy: form the clamp condition beside the arithmetic and apply it as a select, not as a compare-then-select
skills.rationale: A clamp written as compare-then-mux serialises three things: the arithmetic, the comparison, and the selection. The condition usually depends on high bits and overflow flags that the arithmetic produces before its low bits settle.

skills.pattern: select network in series with a long arithmetic path
skills.strategy: speculate every outcome in parallel and select at the end
skills.rationale: The canonical critical path in a pipelined datapath is not the arithmetic alone but a selection standing in front of it: hazard detection, then operand forwarding, then the ALU, in series. Computing each candidate result concurrently and choosing with one late multiplexer takes the selection off the arithmetic path. A carry-select adder exploits the same shape.

skills.pattern: Serial parity chain in CDC-protected domain
skills.strategy: Replace ripple XOR chain with balanced tree
skills.rationale: Tree rebalancing (512 stages → 9 stages) is logically sound via XOR associativity and would reduce critical-path delay. However, parity signals used in cross-clock-domain protection are guarded regions: modifications break SEC equivalence. CDC monitors require exact signal ancestry; tree replication introduces new paths.
skills.example:
// BREAKS EQUIVALENCE:
always @(*) xfrm_par <= par_tree_final ^ cdc_xfrm_from_look[1];  // was: par_chain[XW]

skills.pattern: Serial XOR reduction chain
skills.strategy: Rebalance into binary tree to reduce depth log₂(n)
skills.rationale: XOR tree depth falls from 512 to 9 logic levels, removing ~84 gate delays from the critical path. Equivalence is assured by XOR associativity—reordering the computation preserves the result.

skills.pattern: sign extension replicated before every operand of a wide add
skills.strategy: add the narrow values and sign-extend once at the end
skills.rationale: Sign-extending each product to the accumulator width before adding makes every adder full-width. Adding at the natural width and extending the single result gives the same value with narrower carry chains.

skills.pattern: unpipelined multiplier array in one cycle
skills.strategy: redistribute the existing registers across the array without changing the latency
skills.rationale: When the module already has registers before and after the multiply, the boundary between them can be moved into the array -- retiming -- so each stage carries less depth. Total latency is unchanged, which is what the equivalence check requires.
skills.example:
// move the input register past the partial-product stage rather than
// adding a new one: latency in == latency out.

skills.pattern: wide comparison at the end of the datapath
skills.strategy: precompute the comparison from partial results in parallel with the final arithmetic
skills.rationale: A compare that waits for the full sum adds its own carry chain on top of the datapath's. The deciding bits are usually available earlier -- the sign and the bits above the limit -- so the condition can be formed beside the sum instead of after it.
